summary: Kimberley C. Patton specializes in religious studies. She studied at Harvard University (~1985–1992), where she later served as Assistant Professor in the Comparative and Historical Study of Religion (~1994), and was an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1991).

Kimiaki Tanaka is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo, the University of Oxford, and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. His posts include the University of Tokyo, Eastern Institute, and Beijing Center for Japanese Studies.

Kimmo Koskenniemi is a linguist who studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu. He served as Professor of Computer Linguistics at the University of Helsinki (~1989–2012), where he also directed the Building and Use of Linguistic Technology research community (attested 2015).
Kin Cheung works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shigenori Nagatomo (attested 2017).
King Chung Lo works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed a PhD at the University of Leipzig, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco (2009).
King Pong Chiu specializes in religious studies and Indology. He completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Manchester under doctoral supervisor Jacqueline Suthren Hirst (attested 2014).
Kingsley Muthumuni de Silva was a historian who studied at the University of London (~1958–1961). He served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya (~1969–1995).

Kirby Flower Smith was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University under Gildersleeve, Warren, and Bloomfield. He was a professor at Johns Hopkins (~1889–1918) and Director of the American Academy in Rome.
Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an Indologist. He completed his studies at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti works in philosophy and Indology. He studied under Gopinath Bhattacharya, Ashoke Kumar Gangopadhyaya, and traditional teachers including Madhusudana Nyāyācārya and Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha. He held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitarō Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar who studied at Fourth Higher School and the University of Tokyo under Karl Florenz. He taught at Fourth Higher School, Yamaguchi Higher School, Gakushuin, and served as Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University (1910–1928).

Kiyoaki Okuda is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1969–1973) and held posts as professor at International Buddhist University (attested 1993) and director at Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute (attested 2000).

Kiyoshi Kato was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Otani University under Enga Teramoto, and later held positions at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School (1938).
Kiyoshi Miki was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1917–1920) under Kitarō Nishida. He later held posts at Ryukoku University (~1924–1925) and Otani University (~1925–1927).

Kiyoshi Okano specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies and studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held posts at Kyushu University as an associate professor (attested 2002) and as a professor (attested 2013–2024).
Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Rissho University. He also held posts at Rissho University (attested 1990 and 2001).
Kiyoshi Yabuuchi was a historian and sinologist. He studied at Kyoto University (~1926–1929) and later held positions there (~1935–1970) and at Ryukoku University (~1970–1977).

Kiyotaka Kimura is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, International Buddhist University, Tsurumi University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1982–1991) and under Gerhard Oberhammer (~1987–1991). He held positions at Hokkaido University (~1997–2005), Tohoku University (~2005–2023), and Toyo Bunko.

Kiyozo Kazama is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Harushige Kōzu, and at the University of Vienna. He held faculty posts at Nagoya University, the University of Tokyo, and Hosei University.
